description: The video is a promotional explainer for 'Codos,' an AI platform built by a former McKinsey consultant to help companies figure out what to automate. Presented by a man with glasses speaking into a microphone, the video uses a split-screen format showing him alongside visuals of the software interface and stock office scenes. It explains that Codos starts by conducting 'diagnostic interviews' where a voice agent asks employees to walk through their normal day and how work actually gets done. The system then combines those answers with company documents, messages, and meeting notes from tools like Notion, Slack, Gmail, and HubSpot to create a shared picture of the business. From this, it generates a process map that identifies repetitive tasks, the information they need, and scores them for 'automation fit.' Codos engineers then work with the team to get selected workflows running. The key differentiator highlighted is that instead of asking teams to brainstorm AI uses, Codos looks at the work they already do and finds what can be taken off their plate. The presenter adds credibility by stating he has been running businesses for decades and that the best insights come from people on the ground doing the daily work — which is exactly what Codos aims to leverage. He ends by asking viewers: if AI interviewed your team tomorrow, what boring work would it flag first, and encourages comments and follows for more AI coverage.
